'''Younan Xia''' ({{lang-zh|c=夏幼南}}; born on the 16th of October, 1965) is a Chinese-American [[chemist]], [[materials scientist]], and [[bioengineer]]. He is the [[Bloomberg L.P.|Bloomberg]] [[Bloomberg Distinguished Professorships|Distinguished Professor]] of [[NanoScience|Nanoscience]] and [[Nanotechnology (journal)|Nanotechnology]], with joint appointments in the departments of Materials Science and [[Engineering]] and Biomedical Engineering at [[Johns Hopkins University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Published |first=Annika Weder / |date=2026-02-05 |title=Nanomaterials expert Younan Xia joins Johns Hopkins University |url=https://hub.jhu.edu/2026/02/05/younan-xia-bdp-nanomaterials/ |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=The Hub |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Xia was born in [[Jingjiang, Jiangsu]], China, in 1965. He received his B.S degree in chemical physics from the [[University of Science and Technology of China]] (USTC) in 1987 <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.ustc.edu.cn/|title=University of Science and Technology of China|website=en.ustc.edu.cn|access-date=2019-11-22}}</ref>. He then pursued graduate studies at the Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter until the end of 1990.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://english.fjirsm.cas.cn/|title=Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter}}</ref>

In 1991, he moved to the United States and received an M.S. degree in [[inorganic chemistry]] from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] with [[Alan G. MacDiarmid]] in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.upenn.edu/|title=Home {{!}} Department of Chemistry|website=www.chem.upenn.edu|access-date=2019-11-22}}</ref> He received his PhD degree in physical chemistry from [[Harvard University]] with [[George M. Whitesides]] in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.harvard.edu/home|title=Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology|website=chemistry.harvard.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-11-22}}</ref>

==Research==
The current research of Xia and his group centers on the development of new chemistry, physics, and technological applications of nano-structured materials – a class of materials which feature sizes less than 100 nm.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} His research includes the chemistry and physics of nanomaterial synthesis, the application of nanomaterials to biomedical research, and developing nanomaterials for energy- and environment-related applications.

Xia co-invented soft lithography while he was a PhD student with George M. Whitesides at Harvard University.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Soft Lithography | year = 1998 |author1=Xia, Y. |author2=Whitesides, G. M. |name-list-style=amp | journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition | volume = 37 | pages = 550–575 | doi =10.1002/(SICI)1521-3773(19980316)37:5<550::AID-ANIE550>3.0.CO;2-G| issue = 5| pmid = 29711088 | s2cid = 9026516 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1146/annurev.matsci.28.1.153 | title = Soft Lithography | year = 1998 |author1=Xia, Y. |author2=Whitesides, G. LaMer Award|publisher=Colloidssurfaces.org|access-date=January 26, 2012|archive-date=February 2, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200202105512/http://colloidssurfaces.sites.acs.org/victorklameraward.htm}}</ref>

Xia was named by ''Times Higher Education'' one of the Top 10 chemists (#5) in the world from 1999 to 2009 based on the number of citations per paper.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/top-ten-chemists/409418.article|title=Top ten chemists|date=December 3, 2009 }}</ref> He was also ranked one of the Top 100 material scientists (#4) and top 100 chemists (#35) in the world from 2000 to 2010 based on the number of citations per paper.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100MatSci2000-10/|title=TOP 100 MATERIALS SCIENTISTS}}</ref> He was named one of the world's most influential scientific minds in 2015 in the fields of Chemistry and Materials Science,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&pid=sites&srcid=ZGVmYXVsdGRvbWFpbnxwZXRlcnJlaW5oYXJkaGFuc2VufGd4OjdjNTIyZDM5MmJkNWRhNzQ|title=THE WORLD'S MOST INFLUENTIAL SCIENTIFIC MINDS 2015}}</ref> Best Scientists in the field of Materials Science (ranked #6 in the world and #5 in the United States of America) and Materials Science Leader Award for 2023,<ref>{{Cite web |title=World's Best Materials Science Scientists: H-Index Materials Science Ranking 2024 |url=https://research.com/scientists-rankings/materials-science |access-date=2025-03-17 |website=Research.com |language=en}}</ref> ScholarGPS #2 Ranking in Biomedical Engineering among all academic scholars in the United States (2024).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Highly Ranked Scholars {{!}} Biomedical Engineering |url=https://scholargps.com/highly-ranked-scholars?year=2024&discipline=Biomedical+Engineering |access-date=2025-03-17 |website=ScholarGPS}}</ref> Highly Ranked Scholar— Lifetime— in the Field of Engineering and Computer Science (2025).
